newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures end up strongly.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures end up strongly.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures posted strong gains and ended near session peaks, fueled by followthrough from Monday and technology sector strength.

Nasdaq 100 futures and September S&P 500s rallied sharply, both ending close to their peaks set in afternoon trade. Traders said gains in Dell Computer Corp ahead of its second-quarter earnings cemented the upside index trends.

"It seemed that the Nasdaq was trading at a nice premium all day," an S&P 500 futures trader said. "They never went negative like we did." Earlier Tuesday, September S&Ps fell negative territory but quickly found good buying.
The trader called Tuesday's action a continuation of a much-needed bounce after Friday's huge losses.
He and many other traders said the market has proved that buyers enthusiastically emerge after selloffs in the hopes of capturing more of the U.S. stock bull run.
"I think people are feeling good about buying the dip," the trader said. He noted that Friday's selloff "didn't reach the magical number of 10 percent, but there'll be a lot of money under there."
Another trader said dealers were aggressive buyers throughout the session, with volume moderate overall.
September S&P 500 futures volume was estimated at 63,000 contracts.

Trade was jittery in the first half of the day as players waited for results of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting. The Fed stood pat on rates, as expected, and stocks briefly slipped from their highs after the results.

At the close, Sept S&P 500s rose 12.25 points to 931.00, Russell 2000 rose 5.40 at 417.50, Value Lines rose 9.05 to 839.95, NYSE Composite rose 5.10 to 481.85, NASDAQ rose 28.25 to 1124.50, and Nikkei fell 255.0 to 18,960.00.
